name: Korova Atelier Structured Cape
description:
A mid-length structured cape in heavy wool crepe, cut with architectural precision — the shoulder seams are boned to maintain a distinct silhouette, and the hem is weighted to fall in perfect vertical lines. It fastens at the throat with a single large hook-and-eye in oxidized silver. It comes in black, ivory, and a deep plum. The interior is lined in silk-analog that whispers when you move. This is not a garment for the wind-off-the-lake; it is a garment for being seen.

Korova Atelier produces a small number of pieces per season for Tier 4 and Tier 5 clientele, but the cape has found an unexpected following among geneware users — particularly those with decorative or functional wing modifications, for whom conventional sleeves are impractical. The cape's open structure means it drapes over any body configuration, and the dramatic silhouette complements rather than fights non-standard anatomy. Korova has quietly begun offering a custom cut for wing-span clearance.
what_it_says: You are wealthy enough to wear something impractical and beautiful. You may have geneware. You are absolutely comfortable being looked at.
worn_by: people who have made a decision about who they are
story_hooks: A specific cape was commissioned and then the client never picked it up — the deposit was enormous and Korova's owner is quietly asking questions
Two Tier 5 figures showed up to the same event wearing identical Korova capes — which should be impossible given the limited production run
A the Gray Zone-based performance artist has been wearing a painstakingly hand-sewn imitation of this cape in public, and it's getting more feed attention than the original

physical_description.visual_profile: A dramatic, sharply tailored mid-length cape with an almost architectural presence. The shoulders rise in clean, structured lines that suggest command and precision. The silhouette is imposing but elegant—neither costume nor costume-adjacent, but definitively statement wear. Falls to mid-thigh with controlled, vertical draping that creates a quasi-sculptural effect.
physical_description.fit: Precisely tailored through the shoulders with internal boning that locks the shape in place. The body drapes with intent rather than cling—generous enough to accommodate non-standard physiology (wing modifications, reinforced spinal augments) without excess fabric. The hem is weighted internally to ensure vertical fall regardless of movement or wind.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy wool crepe in a dense weave that holds its structure. The exterior has a subtle matte finish; the interior is lined in silk-analog that creates tactile and acoustic contrast when worn.
physical_description.texture: Exterior reads as smooth but substantial, with a refined nap that catches light subtly. Interior whispers softly with each movement—a deliberate sensory detail. The wool crepe has enough weight to resist wrinkling and to move with authority rather than flutter.
physical_description.color_scheme: Offered in three colorways: pure black (most common), ivory (high-visibility variant), and deep plum (statement choice). Oxidized silver hardware at throat provides restrained metallic accent.
physical_description.closures: Single large hook-and-eye closure in oxidized silver at the throat. Deliberate minimalism—one point of contact, maximum visual impact.
distinctive_features: Internal shoulder boning that maintains silhouette independent of posture or augmentation
Weighted hem for controlled vertical draping
Silk-analog interior lining that produces subtle sound on movement
Open cape structure with no sleeves—accommodates wing modifications and non-standard body configurations
Custom cut variants available for wing-span clearance
Oxidized silver hook-and-eye at throat—understated luxury hardware
Mid-thigh length—formal enough for corporate spaces, dramatic enough for street presence
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 accessible luxury; signals refined taste and discretionary income without corpo excess. The geneware modification market (largely Tier 4-5) has become its secondary audience.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by: modified individuals seeking elegant workarounds for non-standard anatomy; corpo adjacent professionals who value architectural design; street-tier geneware users signaling both body autonomy and sartorial control. The cape's popularity among wing-modified wearers has become a subtle subcultural marker—a way of saying 'I've chosen this modification and I dress accordingly.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Korova pieces are built for longevity and retain their structure through years of wear. Typically seen pristine or gently broken-in, with the silk-analog interior showing subtle wear patterns. Patina on the silver hardware is expected and valued.
